title: A Pinsker-type inequality for the Radon–Nikodym density
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$ with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, and write $f =  rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the (real-valued) Radon–Nikodym density. Suppose the log-likelihood ratio $x \mapsto \log rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable. Then
\[
   rac{1}{2}\left(\int_\Omega \abs{f(x) - 1}\,d
u(x)ight)^{2}
  \;\le\;
  \int_\Omega  igl(f(x)\log f(x) - f(x) + 1 igr)\,d
u(x),
\]
where the left-hand inner integral is the $L^1(
u)$-distance of the density from $1$ and the right-hand integrand is the Kullback–Leibler integrand $t \mapsto t\log t - t + 1$.
hypotheses_covered: mu and nu are probability measures on a measurable space
mu is absolutely continuous with respect to nu
the log-likelihood ratio of mu with respect to nu is mu-integrable
replaced:
If $\mu \ll \nu$ and the log-likelihood ratio $\mathrm{llr}(\mu,\nu)$ is $\mu$-integrable,
then
\[
  \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{densityAbsIntegral}(\mu,\nu)^2
  \;\le\;
  \int \mathrm{klFun}\bigl(\mathrm{rnDensity}(\mu,\nu)(x)\bigr)\,d\nu.
\]
